mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, Exalted is He, وَالْقُرآن: an oath. Its apodosis (answer), according to al-Akhfash, is قد علمنا, with omission of the lām, i.e. "We have certainly known" (لقد علمنا). Al-Zajjāj said the answer is omitted, its implied form being "By the glorious Qur'an, you will surely be resurrected" (والقرآن المجيد لنبعثن), because they denied the resurrection in the verse after it. It is also said that what comes before the oath stands in place of the answer, and that the meaning of ق is "the matter has been decreed" — "By the glorious Qur'an, the matter has been decreed" — so "the matter has been decreed" is the answer, and ق indicated it. It is also said that ق is the name of the mountain, so its implied form is "it is Qāf" (هو ق), and والقرآن المجيد; and the clause stands in place of the answer to the oath.

mekki-muskil:3-3.t: His saying أئذا متْنا: the governing word in إذا is an omitted verb indicated by the speech, because they were people who denied the resurrection, so it is as if they said "Shall we be resurrected when we have died?" (أنبعث إذا متنا). متنا does not govern it, because إذا is annexed to متنا, and the muḍāf ilayhi does not govern the muḍāf.

mekki-muskil:9-9.t: His saying وَحب الحصيد: according to the Kufans this is the annexation of a thing to itself; its implied form according to them is "and the harvested grain" (والحب الحصيد), i.e. the reaped; then the alif and lām were omitted from الحب and it was annexed to الحصيد, which is its naʿt (adjective), and the naʿt is the thing described. According to the Basrans it is a genuine annexation, but it contains the omission of the thing described and the setting up of the adjective in its place; its implied form is "and the grain of the harvested plant" (وحب النبت الحصيد), i.e. the reaped; so النبت was omitted and its adjective set up in its place, and الحب was annexed to الحصيد on this assumption.

mekki-muskil:11-11.t:
His saying رزقا للعباد: a maṣdar (verbal noun); it is also said: a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).
His saying {إِن كل إِلَّا كذب الرُّسُل}: إنْ means ما (not); كل is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and إلا with what follows it is the khabar (predicate). كل means "all of them" (كلهم). Sībawayh related مررت بكلٍّ جالسا ("I passed by all of them sitting"), putting جالسا in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because كل is definite, since its implied form is كلهم. For that reason some grammarians permitted كلُّ منطلق, making كل indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because of the omission of what it is annexed to, treating it like قبل and بعد.

mekki-muskil:16-16.t: His saying توسوس بِهِ: the هاء refers back to ما; it is also said: to الإنسان. And the بـ is in place of إلى.

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying {عَن الْيَمين وَعَن الشمَال قعيد}: the doctrine of Sībawayh is that a قعيد has been omitted from the first part of the speech because the second indicates it. The doctrine of al-Mubarrad is that the قعيد which is in the recitation belongs to the first, but was postponed for latitude of expression, and قعيد was omitted from the second because the first indicates it. The doctrine of al-Akhfash and al-Farrāʾ is that the قعيد which is in the recitation stands for two and more, and there is no omission in the speech.

mekki-muskil:21-21.t:
His saying مَعهَا سائق: [سائق is] a mubtadaʾ (subject) and معها the khabar (predicate), and the clause is in the position of the accusative as an adjective of نفس or of كل. [Translator's note: the edition reads «accusative» (نصب); since نفس and كل are genitive in كل نفس, one would expect «genitive».]
His saying لقد كنت فِي غَفلَة: it is an address to the disbelievers; it is also said: to the disbeliever and the believer; and it is also said: to the Prophet ﷺ.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t: His saying هَذَا مَا لدي عتيد: هذا is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and ما and عتيد are two khabars (predicates). It is also said: ما is the khabar, and عتيد is a badal (substitute) of ما, or a naʿt (adjective) of it, or nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ. In ordinary speech, عتيدًا in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) is permissible.

mekki-muskil:24-24.t:
His saying ألقيا فِي جَهَنَّم: this is an address to the companion (القرين), and it was only put in the dual because He intended repetition, in the sense of "cast, cast" (ألقِ ألقِ). It is also said that it only came in the dual because the Arabs address the single person with the wording of the dual and with the wording of the plural. It is also said that it was put in the dual only because the fewest helpers of one who has standing and honour are two or more, so it was put in the dual on that basis. It is also said that it is only an address to the driver and the guardian (السائق والحافظ).
His saying الَّذِي جعل: الذي is in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of كل, or by [an implied] أعني ("I mean"), or in the position of the nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), or as a mubtadaʾ, with the khabar (predicate) being فألقياه.

mekki-muskil:33-33.t: His saying من خشِي الرَّحْمَن: من is in the position of the genitive (khafḍ) as a badal (substitute) of لكل, or in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being ادخلوها; and the apodosis of the condition is omitted, its implied form being "so it will be said to them: Enter it" (فيقال لهم ادخلوها).

mekki-muskil:44-44.t: His saying سرَاعًا: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the هاء and the ميم in عنهم, and the governing word in it is تشقق. It is also said that the meaning is "so they come out hastening" (فيخرجون سراعا), so it is a ḥāl of the latent pronoun in ويخرجون, and يخرجون is the governing word in it.
